text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.08% today after climbing steeply over the prior three trading days. The decline follows a record diesel price spike driven by refinery shutdowns in Ukraine and Russia, combined with escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—specifically EU sanctions on Iran and South Korea weighing military involvement to keep the Strait of Hormuz open. While higher oil prices typically benefit producers like COP, the refinery disruptions and geopolitical friction appear to have triggered a pullback in energy stocks today, and the stock has given back some of its recent gains.

Crude prices remain elevated (US oil at $91.48/barrel), but the situation is mixed for an integrated oil company: refinery constraints abroad support margins on the crude they pump, yet Middle East tensions and sanctions create unpredictability that can spook investors seeking stability.
